 SINGAPORE – The mercury fell to a low of 22.8 deg C in Scotts Road on Nov 10 amid downpours in the afternoon that triggered a flash flood in West Coast.
 The temperature dip was recorded at 3.02pm, according to data from the Meteorological Service Singapore’s website.
 In earlier posts on social media platform X, national water agency PUB said there was a flash flood at the junction of West Coast Road and West Coast Way, on the afternoon of Nov 10.
 The agency earlier issued an advisory at 2.27pm, urging motorists to avoid West Coast Way for the next hour.
 Afterwards, at 2.35pm, it alerted motorists to a flash flood at the junction of West Coast Road and West Coast Way, near the Japanese Kindergarten.
 In an update at 3pm, the agency said the flood waters had subsided.
 Motorists were also advised to avoid Mackenzie Road (near Bukit Timah Road) for an hour from 2.52pm, the junction of Balmoral Road and Stevens Road for an hour from 2.55pm and Bencoolen Street for an hour from 3pm over the risk of flash floods.
 Singapore’s lowest temperature so far in 2026 was 20.1 deg C , recorded at the Newton weather station on June 12, after heavy downpours ended a long stretch of warm weather linked to the El Nino weather phenomenon.
 In its fortnightly weather forecast, the Met Service on Oct 29 said moderate to heavy thundery showers are expected over parts of the island on most afternoons in the first half of November. 
The showers may extend into the evening on a few of these days, said the weatherman.
 The total rainfall for the first two weeks of November is forecast to be slightly above its long-term average over most parts of the island, it added.
